style_notes: Analog 35mm film photography, Kodak Portra 400 grain structure, heavily muted desaturated palette. Abstract and conceptual — never literal, never illustrative. No people, no faces, no obvious religious iconography. Evoke emotional and theological truth through texture, light, shadow, and negative space alone. Think Alabaster Books meets Kinfolk magazine: spare, intimate, unhurried. Objects minimal or absent. Light does the storytelling.
color_palette: Cold mist gray, weathered willow, mud brown, ash, hot pale stone, dried clay-red, bone white — heavily desaturated with analog film warmth

images.title: By the Rivers of Babylon
images.concept: Exile by water — willows weeping, harps hung in silence, the captors' demand for song
images.imageAlt: A bare weeping willow branch hanging over still gray-brown water, an empty lute case lying on the muddy bank below
images.prompt: 35mm analog film photograph, low angle view of a single weeping willow branch hanging bare over still gray-brown water, an empty wooden lute case lying open on the muddy bank just below, no figures, the water perfectly motionless reflecting overcast sky, cold mist softening edges, heavy Kodak Portra 400 grain, deeply muted palette of dust gray, bleached willow, mud, charcoal sky, the silence after the song refused, Alabaster Books aesthetic, 16:9

images.title: Remembering Jerusalem
images.concept: Vowed memory — fidelity through distance, the hand stilled rather than forget
images.imageAlt: A doorway looking out from shadow onto a sun-baked road leading toward distant pale stone walls, a single palm-print pressed into the threshold dust
images.prompt: 35mm analog film photograph, doorway-frame perspective looking out from a shadowed interior onto an empty sun-baked road that disappears toward distant pale stone walls on the horizon, a single open palm-print pressed clearly into the dust of the threshold stone, no figures, hot still air, heavy Kodak Portra 400 grain, muted bleached palette of bone stone, dust, hot pale sky, the unmistakable mark of a hand that remembered, Alabaster Books aesthetic, 16:9

images.title: Vengeance
images.concept: Terrible justice surrendered to God — rage given language, the aftermath visible
images.imageAlt: Scattered broken red-clay pottery sherds against the base of a weathered wall, fragments arranged as if mid-cascade, late afternoon shadow
images.prompt: 35mm analog film photograph, low view of scattered broken red-clay pottery sherds against the base of a weathered terracotta wall, fragments arranged as if caught mid-cascade, late afternoon shadow falling across them at a steep angle, no figures, no violence depicted but the aftermath unmistakable, heavy Kodak Portra 400 grain, muted palette of dried blood-red clay, charcoal shadow, dust, the silence after a cry that won't be unheard, the bare hard fact of what was wished, Alabaster Books aesthetic, 16:9
